passage: Counselling note, Thursday. Tarun, a second-year student, came in after the committee's notice went up on the board. He said his project guide, Anand, keeps making remarks about how he looks and, twice this month, put a hand on his back after he had stepped away. Tarun kept apologising for "making a fuss" and asked whether he had somehow encouraged it. I told him plainly that it is not his fault and that he did nothing to invite it. He had already saved the messages and written the dates in his phone. We went through how to file a written complaint with the internal committee, and I offered to sit with him when he submits it. He agreed to tell his sister tonight as well. I will check in with him on Monday.

qa.q: How many times this month did Anand put a hand on Tarun's back?
qa.a: Anand did it twice this month.

qa.q: Why did Tarun keep apologising and ask whether he had encouraged it?
qa.a: He seems to fear that he caused it or is making too much of it, and the counsellor's plain reply speaks to that fear.

qa.q: What steps moved Tarun toward reporting?
qa.a: He saved the messages and dates, learned how to file a written complaint with the internal committee, and will have the counsellor beside him and tell his sister.

qa.q: What might it mean for Tarun that the counsellor offers to sit with him when he submits the complaint?
qa.a: It means he does not have to face the process alone, and a trusted adult is sharing it.

grounding: A student is affected by a guide's unwanted comments and touch; the response is recognising it as wrong, keeping records and reporting.

passage:
To the Internal Committee, Department of Physics
I am reporting behaviour by my project guide, Dr. Gautam Sinha, that has made me afraid to attend meetings.
Since August he has commented on my clothes in almost every meeting ("That colour suits you, you should wear it more often for me"). On 12 September and again on 3 October he kept his hand on my back while reading my screen, though I moved away both times. On 3 October I said clearly, "Please don't touch me." He laughed.
I wrote down each date and his words the same day. The notes are attached. My friend Shruti was present on 12 September.
I wondered whether I was overreacting. I'm not. Please act, and assign me a different guide meanwhile.
Kiran Kumari, MSc Physics, second year
Reply, same evening, 6:40 p.m.: Thank you, Kiran. This is not your fault. A committee member will meet you tomorrow at 10 a.m.; you need not attend meetings with Dr. Sinha meanwhile.

qa.q: On which dates did Dr. Sinha put his hand on Kiran's back?
How has Dr. Sinha's behaviour made Kiran feel?
qa.a: Afraid to attend meetings, and at times doubting whether she was overreacting.
Notes written the same day with dates and his exact words, a named witness, and a clear request for action and a different guide.
The same evening it says this is not her fault, sets a meeting for the next morning, and spares her any meetings with Dr. Sinha meanwhile.

grounding: Shows a guide's unwanted comments and touch, recognising it as wrong, keeping records and reporting to the internal committee, with the message that it is never her fault.

passage:
I never told you this properly, Meenal. Last year my dance mentor at the academy, Dhruv sir, started texting me late at night. "You looked beautiful in practice." "Don't tell the others I'm giving you extra attention." Then at a rehearsal he held my waist far longer than the step needed, and I froze.
I told myself it was my fault for being friendly. I stopped eating before practice. I almost quit dance.
One evening my mother saw me flinch at a message and asked. I showed her everything. She didn't shout. She said, "This is not your fault. We keep every message." That same night she emailed the academy's director with the screenshots, and the next morning we went together to the academy's complaints committee.
He was removed from teaching while they looked into it. I moved to another batch. I still dance.
So, from me, Shalini: if someone older asks you to keep their attention secret, that's the moment to tell someone.

qa.q: What did Dhruv sir text late at night?
qa.a: "You looked beautiful in practice" and "Don't tell the others I'm giving you extra attention."

qa.q: How did Shalini feel after the rehearsal?
qa.a: Frozen and ashamed, wrongly blaming herself, so much that she stopped eating before practice and almost quit.

qa.q: What did Shalini's mother do that same night?
qa.a: She stayed calm, said it was not Shalini's fault, kept every message, emailed the academy's director with screenshots, and went with Shalini to the complaints committee the next morning.
Dhruv sir was removed from teaching during the inquiry, and Shalini moved batches and kept dancing.

grounding: Illustrates a mentor's unwanted comments and touch, a same-night report by a trusted adult to the academy, and the message that it is never the young person's fault.
